facts.raw_span: A 69-year-old Japanese man presented with pain and a 10-mm polypoid mass on the left lower gingiva
He had undergone chemoradiotherapy 15 years earlier for squamous cell carcinoma of the left buccal mucosa, with no recurrence until now
He denied tobacco or alcohol use
trismus was present
a rough-surfaced polypoid lesion in the left lower molar gingiva covered by a whitish pseudomembrane
Panoramic radiography showed a moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption
Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated an enhancing soft-tissue mass with irregular mandibular bone destruction
A biopsy specimen showed loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells in a fibrin-rich edematous stroma alongside inflammatory cells
The spindle cells had basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses; many contained neutrophils within cytoplasmic vacuoles
Immunohistochemical staining revealed that the spindle cells were positive for vimentin, α-smooth muscle actin, p63, p53, and CD68, but negative for pan-cytokeratin and other epithelial markers
Ki-67 labeling index was approximately 50%
These findings prompted consideration of a malignant spindle cell process

concepts.why: The presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells, positive immunohistochemical staining for vimentin and negative for pan-cytokeratin, and a history of squamous cell carcinoma suggest sarcomatoid carcinoma.

The biopsy specimen showing loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells, and positive immunohistochemical staining for CD68, suggests malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
The presence of atypical spindle cells with basophilic cytoplasm and positive immunohistochemical staining for α-smooth muscle actin suggests leiomyosarcoma.

The biopsy specimen showing loose granulation tissue with scattered atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells, and positive immunohistochemical staining for vimentin and α-smooth muscle actin, suggests inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor.
The presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells, positive immunohistochemical staining for p63 and p53, and a history of squamous cell carcinoma suggest sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma.
It explains the moth-eaten pattern of mandibular bone resorption and the enhancing soft-tissue mass with irregular mandibular bone destruction.

rationales.F02: History of squamous cell carcinoma increases the likelihood of sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F06: Moth-eaten pattern of bone resorption is suggestive of aggressive bone destruction, seen in various sarcomas and carcinomas.
rationales.F08: Presence of atypical spindle and pleomorphic cells is indicative of a malignant process.
rationales.F09: Basophilic cytoplasm, bizarre nuclei, and atypical mitoses in spindle cells are characteristic of malignant cells.
rationales.F10: Immunohistochemical staining pattern is consistent with a malignant spindle cell process, such as sarcomatoid carcinoma or malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
rationales.F11: High Ki-67 labeling index indicates a high proliferation rate, typical of malignant tumors.
rationales.F12: Consideration of a malignant spindle cell process is based on the combination of clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of squamous cell carcinoma and the presence of atypical spindle cells with immunohistochemical staining positive for p63, a marker often associated with squamous cell carcinoma, support this diagnosis.
